On a case still drifting at 300 that inconsistency enters the fit as if it were grid error.

iteration_consistency_audit.reproduction_check: both rebuilt meshes reproduce their stored cell counts exactly (14,714 and 66,302) and their stored Cd exactly at the 180-iteration window (0.4709343 and 0.4213963), so the rebuild is the same measurement, not a new one

refit.reason_after: the observed order p = 7.082 falls outside the credible range 0.5 to 2.5

the_real_obstacle.statement: the production rung is still drifting at 300 iterations by more than the entire grid increment the observed order is fitted to. Coarse and medium are settled at 300 (final-window 2-sigma 2.41e-04 each, halves-drift below 4e-04); production is not (2-sigma 1.21e-03, halves-drift 1.75e-03). A FOURTH RUNG CANNOT FIX THIS. A finer rung makes the finest increment smaller, driving the signal further beneath the noise, not above it. The prerequisite is iterative convergence on the production mesh.

recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.says_nothing_against_the_solves: THIS SAYS NOTHING AGAINST THE UNDERLYING SOLVES. recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.one_way_door: The affected rows move TOWARD NOT A RESULT, which CLAUDE.md rule 5 permits -- never back. In rule 5 own words the gate "can only turn a PASS or GATE FAIL INTO NOT A RESULT, never the reverse." Nothing here turns any NOT A RESULT back into a PASS.

recipe_fork_ruling_2026_08_25.instrument_stated_limit: similarity_failures() treats ANY change of a block grading as a similarity failure ("regraded cells are not scaled cells"). That is CORRECT for the uniform-background snappyHexMesh ladders this sweep covers and WRONG for a correctly-built GRADED ladder, which must change its grading string as it refines precisely in order to keep the first cell scaling. F12 repaired RAE 2822 ladder is exactly such a family, so running recipe_audit.py against it would report a SPURIOUS FORK. A check that overstates its reach is worse than none. See section 5 of the record.
